interpretation.direct_comparison: Both actual source checkpoints (SmolLM2 GGUF Q8_0 and TinyLLM PyTorch/SentencePiece) plus the v3_0 student and preservation-release v3_1 student were loaded from their exact local ZIPs and evaluated on the same frozen English and Chinese strings. All 16 English and 8 Chinese documents are scored up to 96 UTF-8 bytes each. Bits per UTF-8 byte is the cross-tokenizer normalized metric; native-token perplexity and next-token accuracy are not compared as identical units across tokenizers.
interpretation.mechanistic_scope: The study includes component inspection, hidden-state and attention observation where available, and post-block ablations/scaling. It does not establish complete circuit discovery or mechanistic equivalence.
interpretation.reconstruction_status: The selected v3_1 release preserves the v3_0 text-generation path exactly and adds a separately trained observation-view router. The joint-finetune candidate is retained as a counterexample because it degraded held-out language modeling. The sidecar obtains 4/16 eight-way accuracy on the reserved classification test (25% versus 12.5% uniform chance), which is preliminary small-sample evidence, not robust classification. Neither student is a capacity-matched or mechanistically equivalent reconstruction of either source.
counterexamples_to_overclaim: TinyLLM is a Chinese-oriented custom Llama-like 8-layer model; English task generation is out-of-domain and must be interpreted accordingly.
A finite set of layer interventions cannot assign semantic meaning to a layer or establish full causal completeness.
The 54,536-parameter v3_0 base and 55,568-parameter v3_1 sidecar are not capacity-matched to either the 76.9M- or 134.5M-parameter source model.
The v3_1 joint-finetune candidate worsened held-out bit-per-byte and is not the selected release checkpoint; it is retained as counter-evidence.
